steps: Uncrate & fit side panels

Remove the crate top, supports and plastic cover; unbolt the pallet lag bolts with a 7/16" (12mm) wrench. Hook the side panels' front tabs into the bracket slots, pull back and screw on, with fibre washers on enamel panels.
Connect the A/C adapter

Take the adapter from inside the unit, plug its barrel plug into the control board and the adapter into a wall outlet; don't route the cord beneath the heater. Optional battery box: follow its own instructions.
Thermocouple guard & agitator
Lift the thermocouple guard out of the flue collar, remove the cardboard holding the flue gas agitator (check its rear pin is in place), then refit the guard with all three ends seated.
Floor protector
Continuous non-combustible protection: USA 16" front and 8" to the sides of the door opening; Canada 18" firing side and 8" other sides; also under the connector plus 2" each side.
Clearances & alcove
Place the stove to the rating-label clearances; use a listed double-wall connector for close clearances. Alcove: 7' minimum height, 36" maximum depth.
Chimney & connector
6" flue to a UL-103HT / ULC-S629 listed or lined masonry chimney: 15 feet minimum system height, 3 feet above the roof, two feet above anything within 10 feet. Never share a flue.

Flue6 inches, same as the stove outlet
System height15 feet (4.6 m.) minimum, from base of appliance
Termination3 feet (1 m.) above roof, two feet (0.6 m.) above the highest projection within 10 feet (3 m.)

Double-wall: use a listed double-wall connector and install chimney and connector to their maker's requirements. Single-wall: six inch 24 gauge black pipe, clean and new, as short and straight as possible, crimped (male) ends down, 3 sheet metal screws at every joint and collar.

The connector must not pass through an attic, roof space, closet or similar concealed space, floor or ceiling; a combustible wall pass-through must follow CAN/CSA-B365 or NFPA 211. Offsets: screw every connector, elbow and chimney joint with at least three sheet metal screws and support the chimney with its maker's listed offset support.
Install the venting
Plumb-bob the flue centre to ceiling and roof, check joists and rafters, install the listed chimney to the rain cap, then fit the connector crimped end into the collar with three screws.

1. Select the position from the clearances; place the floor protection and stove.
  2. Hang a plumb-bob over the exact centre of the flue to mark the ceiling and roof holes.
  3. Check for floor joists, ceiling joists and rafters; adjust and reconfirm clearances.
  4. Install the listed chimney from the ceiling through to the rain cap per its directions.
  5. Slip the connector's crimped edge inside the stove collar; secure through the collar holes with three screws.
  6. Stack the remaining lengths to the chimney with the manufacturer's approved adapter; a slip section helps.

Through a combustible wall (NFPA 211-2013)

System A12 in. (305mm) to combustibles · brick wall, fireclay liner
System B9 in. (229mm) to combustibles · insulated listed chimney length
System C6 in. (152mm) to combustibles · ventilated thimble, glass fiber insulation
System D2 in. (51mm) to combustibles · insulated chimney length as pass-through

Maintain the vapour barrier wherever the chimney penetrates to the exterior. For an up-and-out connection the drawings call for a 12" (305mm) minimum first section of pipe; give it as much vertical length as possible, as the unit may be harder to start.
Combustion air
Room air enters through the Ash Box Enclosure. For outside air, fit the 4" Intake Starter, run 4" metal flex through the floor or the wall behind, and secure the stove to the structure.
Mobile home extras
Lag the legs or pedestal to the floor with two 1/4" x 2" or longer screws; listed double-wall connector only, no horizontal connector; outside air required; never in a sleeping room.
Firebricks
Rear wall first, then each side wall, then the floor, per the brick layout (Figure 24); one full-size A brick is a spare. Replace any broken or missing bricks.

1. Rear wall: two A bricks behind the right brick-rail tab, slid to the centre; on the left, two A bricks with one B between them.
  2. Each side wall: E brick up into the back corner with an A beneath it, then a B up under the baffle tube box with two A bricks beneath.
  3. Floor: an A in each corner and one B; an A in front of the left rear A; a D behind the ash dump; a C in front of the ash dump; two A on the right; the last D in the centre in front of the B.
A9" X 4 1/2" X 1 1/4"
B2" X 9" X 1 1/4"
C4 3/8" X 4 3/8" X 1 1/4"
D2" X 4 7/16" X 1 1/4"
E4 7/16" X 3 1/4" X 1 1/4"

One full-size A brick is left over as a spare. Firebrick set: part 80002938.

panels.title: Excess creosote / dirty glass
items: Wood too wet → use dry wood
Air turned down too soon → wait for a good bed of coals and charred wood
Draft too low → plugged or restricted flue, wrong chimney height or diameter; provide outside air
Dirty glass: door gasket leakage → replace gasket, check door latch

panels.title: Low heat output
items: Wood may be wet → use drier wood
Fire too small → build a larger fire, open the draft control
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean

panels.title: Won't burn overnight
items: Air control set too high → set it lower
Not enough wood → unsplit wood is preferred
Draft too high → excessive chimney height and/or diameter

panels.title: Stove won't burn
items: Combustion air blocked → check the outside air supply for obstructions
Room air cover still on → check that it is removed
Chimney plugged or restricted → inspect and clean

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
You light this stove by hand. The air control sits beneath the ash lip at the front.

  1. Slide the air control to High, all the way to the left, and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the firebox. Crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it, then add a few pieces of large kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open a crack, about 1/2" to 1", until the kindling is fully in flames. Never leave the stove alone with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small pieces of wood and close the door.
  5. Begin normal burning once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred.
Never start or "freshen up" a fire with gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other chemical or volatile liquid.

Your first few fires

The paint bakes on during the first 2–3 fires, giving off smoke and fumes that may bother some people. Ventilate well: open all windows and doors, and follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with your stove. Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures. Don't disconnect them.

Build the fire directly on the firebricks. Don't use a grate or andirons.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sits beneath the ash lip. Facing the stove, it slides from Low (right) to High (left), with Medium about in the middle. Any position in between sets the burn rate and heat output.

Low: overnight and long burns

Unsplit logs work best. Char the wood completely on High first, then slowly turn the control down to Low.

High: lighting and reloading

Burn on High for about 10–15 minutes after loading, or until the wood is fully charred. Don't leave it on High for long periods, or you risk over-firing the stove.

To reload

  1. Turn the air to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff out.
  3. Load logs (up to 18" long) parallel to the front, with gaps so air can flow between them. Don't stack wood so high that opening the door becomes hazardous.

After an overnight burn: rake the hot embers to the front, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to High. Once the wood has charred, reset the control.

Have the optional blower? When the air control is on Low, run the blower on Low too, or the fire may go out.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood burns cleaner and more efficiently than softwood or green, freshly cut wood. Logs of 17" are ideal; 18" is the maximum.

  • Season wood for six months or more. Store it under cover, away from open flame or heat.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.
  • Never try an overnight burn with green or wet wood.

Test your wood

Put a large piece on a good, large bed of coals. Burning on more than one side within one minute: it's dry. Turns black and lights within three minutes: it's damp. Sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes: too wet to burn.

Never burn

Salt-water wood, treated wood, garbage, coal or charcoal, solvents, yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything containing rubber, plastic or asbestos, construction debris, petroleum products, paints, plywood, particleboard, cardboard or paper products. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting. Never barbecue in the stove: charcoal can make large amounts of carbon monoxide, which can kill.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Only remove ashes when the stove is cold. When ash is 3" to 4" deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the excess. Leave about 1" on the firebox floor to help keep a hot charcoal bed.

Using the ash dump

  1. The handle is behind the Lower Grill, under the ash lip on the left. Pull the grill up to unlock it, then tip it towards you.
  2. Pull the handle out 1/2" and turn it clockwise. This unlocks the ash dump so it can open.
  3. Hold the handle open while you pull ashes into the opening. Avoid large embers; they still hold heat.
  4. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Make sure the ash dump door is properly engaged, then fill the cavity with the remaining ash, level with the firebox floor.
  5. Lift out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container, and put it back so it's seated properly.
Never burn with the ash dump door open. It creates a hazardous condition.

Storing ashes

Use a metal container with a tight-fitting lid, set on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn. Keep the ashes sealed in it until every cinder has cooled, and don't put other waste in it.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
If the glass darkens from slow burning or poor wood, clean it with fireplace glass cleaner once the stove is cold.

  • Never clean the glass while it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that might scratch.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion and dry wood, so your pipes and chimney are relatively clean. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. It's building up at least as fast in the chimney.

Protect the glass

  • Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close it.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before using the stove. Use only 18" x 10-1/4" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.
Keeps getting dirty? The troubleshooting chart points to wet wood, turning the air down too soon, low draft, or a leaking door gasket.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar and vapours that condense in the cool chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot.

Prevent a chimney fire

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months in the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Check daily at first, until you learn how often cleaning is needed. Mild weather may need weekly cleaning; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Burn small loads (two or three logs, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load) with the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes, then turn it down.
  • Burn dry wood, and don't turn the stove down too quickly after loading.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get everyone ready to leave, with a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department, and keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before your next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks, and check the roof and combustibles around the chimney.

safety.title: Safety & over-firing
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; touching it can burn skin.
  • Hot glass will burn. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning; open it only to add wood. Keep the ash dump closed too.
  • Keep gasoline, kerosene, lighter fluid and similar liquids well away from the stove.
  • Keep furniture, newspapers, stored wood and other combustibles out of the clearance space and the area you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended near the stove.
  • Teach everyone in your household how to run the stove safely and what to do in a chimney fire.

Signs of over-firing

A glowing red top, vent pipe, chimney or connector means the stove is over-firing. Pushing it past its design output can permanently damage the stove and chimney, can be hazardous, and may void the warranty. Don't run it on High for long periods. An uncontrollable burn points to too much draft; smoke leaking from the stove or pipe joints points to too little.

Never alter the air control or its factory-set minimum burn rate. It's hazardous, against federal regulations, and voids the warranty.

care.title: Regular checks & upkeep
care.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and bad warping.

WeeklyFirebricks for cracks; door gasket for sagging, placement or damage
MonthlyBrick rails and tabs, air riser tube, back of the airwash chamber, baffle locking pin, boost tube cover holes
When the chimney is cleanedBaffle board and blanket, baffle and baffle gasket, top heat shield and bolts, brick rails, air riser tube
Every six monthsVacuum the optional blower's grill openings
  • Some baffle warping, up to 1/4", is normal. Replace the baffle if it warps more, cracks or breaks.
  • The door gasket needs only light pressure to seal. Replace it with the kit from your Pacific Energy dealer when needed.
  • Replace broken or missing firebricks.
  • Keep the boost-air area at the front of the firebox clear of ash.
  • Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer for repairs and replacements.
Never run the stove with the baffle, tubes, insulation or flue gas agitator removed. Call your dealer about any damage: running with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty.

power.title: Power, outages & batteries
power.html:
The stove's control board is powered by an A/C adapter plugged into a wall outlet. Don't route the power cord beneath the stove.

Reset after a flicker

If the power flickers, the control board may freeze up. Unplug the adapter from the wall, wait at least 30 seconds, then plug it back in. Whenever you unplug the stove for any reason, wait the same 30 seconds before plugging it back in.

In a power cut

Until power is restored (or the batteries are replaced), the stove still runs within safe and certified limits using the manual air control at the front. With the optional battery box, it stays fully functional during an outage. Batteries last an estimated 5–7 days under continuous use.

Changing the batteries

  1. The battery box sits low on the right side panel as you face the stove, held on by magnets. Lift it off so the battery cover faces up. Don't pull on the wires to the control board.
  2. Release the catch at the end and lift off the cover.
  3. Replace the old batteries with new ones.
  4. Refit the cover and put the box back on the side panel.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's wood products warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 years, parts and laborAny defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches
Not in lifetime coverageFirebox rails, heat shields
Not warrantedFirebrick, gaskets, ceramic fiber blankets

What can void it

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.
  • Signs of improper use such as excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals).
  • Tampering with the air control, burning salt-water wood or garbage, or over-firing.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. Register your stove at pacificenergy.net/register; the serial number is on the certification label and the cover of your installation manual.

specOutput.title: Heat output & wood size
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output13,240 to 29,536 Btu/hr
Ideal wood length17 inches
Maximum wood length18 inches
FuelSeasoned cord wood (solid fuel only)

The range is based on CSA B415 efficiency and burn rates from the low and high EPA tests using Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. Load parallel to the stove front, directly on the firebricks: no grate, andirons or elevated fire.

specEmis.title: Emissions & efficiency
specEmis.html:
EPA certified emissions1.6 g/hr
HHV tested efficiency73%
LHV tested efficiency79%

Meets the EPA 2020 particulate emission standards using cribwood, tested to EPA Method 28R. Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415: HHV includes the energy required to vaporize the water in the fuel; LHV assumes the moisture is already in a vapour state.

The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered. Altering it, or operating the stove other than as the manual instructs, is against federal regulations.

specFlue.html:

Keep the flue the same size as the 6" outlet; reducing or increasing it may hurt performance. Never connect to a flue serving another appliance or to any air distribution duct, and never install in a fireplace.

Single-wall connector: as short and straight as possible, six inch 24 gauge black pipe, clean and new, crimped ends down, 3 sheet metal screws at every joint and collar. It must not pass through an attic, roof space, closet, concealed space, floor or ceiling; wall pass-throughs follow CAN/CSA-B365 or NFPA 211. Overall dimensions appear only as a drawing (Figure 2, p. 13).

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
The stove may go on a combustible floor with continuous non-combustible ember protection extending:

USA16" (406 mm) to the front, 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening
Canada18" (457 mm) on the firing side, 8" (203 mm) to the other sides
Under the connectorRequired, plus 2" (51 mm) beyond each side
Minimum size · USA34 5/8"(880mm) wide × 37 3/8"(949mm) deep
Minimum size · Canada45"(1.14m) wide × 47 5/8"(1.21m) deep

The U.S. drawing specifies a Type 1 floor protector approved to UL1618, minimum 20GA steel. Don't obstruct the space beneath the heater.

The rating label (p. 3) also shows floor protection as a lettered drawing; check it against these figures.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
ResidentialRoom air, or outside air (optional)
Mobile homeOutside air supply required (outside air kit)
Duct4"(100mm) i.d. metal flex pipe
Outside inlet4" (102mm) diameter with rodent screen; hooded vent or 90° elbow turned down

Through the floor: cut a hole for 4" metal flex behind where the unit will sit, attach the 4" Intake Starter to the Ash Box Enclosure and connect the flex. Draw from a ventilated crawl space or extend the duct outdoors; a well-ventilated crawl space needs no extension. From behind: 4"(100mm) air intake through the wall behind the unit, Intake Starter over the hole in the rear of the Ash Box enclosure, metal flex between them.

Residential outside air requires securing the unit to the structure so the duct can't dislodge. On room air the stove draws through the opening in the Ash Box Enclosure. If it won't burn, the troubleshooting chart says to check the outside air supply for obstructions and that the room air cover is removed.

Anything that causes negative pressure can pull gases or fumes into the living area. In extreme cold at very slow burn rates the exposed chimney can ice up; if it blocks, flue gases may enter the living space.

specBlower.title: Optional blower
specBlower.html:
KitPart # 11140001
Electrical rating (p. 27)115 volts AC-1.02 amps
Rating label (p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP
Fan output160 CFM
Confirm the blower current: the manual gives 1.02 amps in the Optional Blower section (p. 27) and 1.0 AMP on the rating label (p. 3).

Three-prong power cord; can be installed at any time per the kit's instructions. Route the cord away from the heater, never beneath it. Auto (rocker switch on the side of the fan housing): the fan starts as the stove heats and shuts off after the fire is out and the unit has cooled. Man: bypasses the temperature sensor and runs until switched off. With the air control on L, run the blower on Low or the unit may go out. Vacuum the grill openings at least every six months.

conflicts.issue: Optional blower current: the rating label gives FAN ELECTRICAL RATING 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP; the Optional Blower section gives 115 volts AC-1.02 amps.

Connector clearances: the rating label lists side wall / back wall / corner to connector as 23-1/2 / 15 / 17 5/8 in. (single wall) and 19 1/2 / 8 / 12 5/8 in. (double wall). The residential clearance drawing (p. 19) prints 26 1/2, 20 5/8, 18 in. (single wall) and 22 1/2, 15 5/8, 11 in. (double wall); the mobile home drawing (p. 26) prints 22 1/2, 15 5/8, 11 in. Each drawing value is 3 in. more than a label value, so the drawings may measure to the flue centreline, but the text does not say. The stove-to-wall values (12, 8 single wall; 8, 5, 3 double wall) also appear on the drawings.

review.notes: The p. 3 'Efficiency and BTU Output' table is printed sideways and the text extraction scrambles it; label/value pairs were matched by their shared column in the manual's layout text (HHV 73%, LHV 79%, EPA BTU output 13,240 to 29,536 btu/hr, emissions 1.6 grams per hour, ideal 17 / maximum 18 inches, fuel seasoned cord wood). Rating-label clearances A-F use the letter definitions printed on the label; the single-wall vs double-wall columns follow the label headings and layout. The label's single-wall back-wall and corner-to-connector figures (15 in., 17 5/8 in.) are below its own general 18 in. single-wall connector minimum; the label marks that column 'as tested - pipe shield may be required by local authorities'. Not transcribed (drawing only): overall dimensions (Figure 2, p. 13), clearance drawings (Figures 16 and 23, pp. 19 and 26) beyond the conflict note, venting drawings (Figures 17-18, pp. 22-23) beyond their printed notes, the label's G/H/I floor-protector letters (p. 3) and the brick layout figure (only the written brick steps and size table are used). Floor-protector mm conversions differ slightly between the label (16 in. / 405 mm, 18 in. / 450 mm) and p. 18 (406 mm, 457 mm); inch values agree. Warranty heading reads 'LTD Lifetime Coverage (10 years)'; shown as printed. The manual lists a control board, A/C adapter (12V wall adapter), thermocouples and a motor control assembly but never explains what the electronic control does in normal use; the guide repeats only its plug-in, reset and power-failure notes. Battery type for the optional battery box is not stated. The label line 'CO emissions are 1.6 grams per minute' was left out (looks doubtful; worth checking with the maker). No error-code table; codes left empty. Pages 34-35 are blank. Label text is bilingual; no French-only content. Catalog says 'Not for sale in the USA', but the manual is certified for Canada and U.S.A. and gives U.S. requirements; confirm availability before selling in Wisconsin. Catalog heating area, cordwood maximum output, burn time, firebox volume, glass/view area and non-catalytic type are not stated in the manual, so they could not be checked.
